summary: Riverside County, CA lookout built for the Cleveland National Forest in 1914; exact site and removal date unknown; no source describes what remains.

facts.design: Cabin on a short open timber tower; register says it appears to be a modified California Plan 4A or an original DuBois 12x12 design
facts.status_note: Register gives the removal date and the exact site as unknown; no source found that describes what remains
facts.agency: US Forest Service, San Bernardino National Forest (San Jacinto Ranger District)

events.note: Built for the Cleveland National Forest

notes_for_editor: History rests on the register page and one Forest Service crew history; no staffing or fire records were found within the search budget. The FS page calls the 1930s camp a California Conservation Corps camp, and the story uses that wording; no other source was checked. The register says Vista Grande Fire Station and the FS page says Vista Grande Guard Station; not reconciled, so the story names each as its source gives it. The register photo caption (c. 1920s, courtesy Cleveland National Forest) has no image URL in the cached page, so no photo entry was added.
